item.title: Ministry of Health begins major hospital bed upgrade programme
item.description: More beds are expected to be delivered to hospitals around the country as the Health Ministry has started the implementation of a nationwide hospital bed upgrade programme, with 1,502 units of medical furniture, including beds and other equipment. item.content:encoded:
More beds are expected to be delivered to hospitals around the country as the Health Ministry has started the implementation of a nationwide hospital bed upgrade programme, with 1,502 units of medical furniture, including beds and other equipment.

While responding to questions from Opposition MP Alvick Maharaj on the progress of the hospital bed upgrade programme, Minister for Health Dr Ratu Atonio Lalabalavu says a total of 779 general hospital beds have been approved under the tender process, with 338 allocated for the Central Division , 312 for the Western Division, 117 for the Eastern Division, and 12 for the Northern Division .

H e says in the Western Division, Nadi Hospital will receive 84 beds, 74 beds for Sigatoka Hospital, 43 for Lautoka Hospital, and Tavua Hospital will receive 29 beds.

In the Northern Division, Labasa Hospital will receive specialised electric beds for its Critical Care Unit and operating theatres.

In the Central Division, the CWM Hospital will receive new beds for critical areas, including the Children’s Ward, Labour Ward, Postnatal Ward, Birthing Unit, and Intensive Care Unit.

He says Tamavua Hospital will also receive 39 beds for its Dermatology and Tuberculosis wards.

Dr Lalabalavu says the wider procurement package will also include 75 paediatric beds, 40 psychiatric beds, 23 five-function hydraulic cardiac beds, 58 emergency beds, 25 patient transfer trolleys, 150 electric examination couches, 76 scoop stretchers, and 372 wheelchairs.

He says the phased approach over three years will allow biomedical technicians to properly inspect, assemble, and maintain the new equipment.

Insert: we are dedicated to our health system KK 19th Aug

Dr Lalabalavu says these approvals were secured in the last financial year for a major tender to procure medical beds and equipment, ma rking the beginning of a multi-year initiative to replace outdated beds across most health facilities in Fiji because, many health facilities have been operating with ageing infrastructure, including patient beds that have exceeded their economic and clinical lifespan.

He says the programme is part of the Government’s commitment to improving healthcare infrastructure and ensuring patients receive treatment in facilities that meet modern clinical standards.

When questioned about overcrowding at the Emergency Department at the CWM Hospital, Dr Lalabalavu says the expansion of the Accident and Emergency area is included under the Fiji Infrastructure and Transport project.

When asked about the responsibility for maintaining hospital equipment, including wheelchairs and other fixtures, Dr Lalabalavu says responsibility lies with everyone, including patients and staff responsible for managing health facilities.

He says nursing supervisors in wards are responsible for monitoring equipment and reporting any damage or misuse.

While responding to concerns about patients waiting without beds at the Emergency Department, he says the issue was mainly due to space constraints.

item.title: Students still waiting for subsidised bus cards as Term 3 approaches
item.description: Students who have been waiting for government-funded bus cards for months could face further uncertainty as Term 3 approaches, with concerns raised in Parliament over delays in the National Transport Assistance Scheme. The issue was raised in Parliament today following a question to the Minister for Education, Aseri Radrodro, about how the Ministry plans to ensure government funded student cards a
item.content:encoded:
Students who have been waiting for government-funded bus cards for months could face further uncertainty as Term 3 approaches, with concerns raised in Parliament over delays in the National Transport Assistance Scheme.

The issue was raised in Parliament today following a question to the Minister for Education, Aseri Radrodro, about how the Ministry plans to ensure government funded student cards are topped up on time in the future.

Radrodro says that eligible students must apply for transport assistance through their schools before the beginning of each school year.

He says applications are then assessed and verified by school heads before being processed by the Ministry.

Radrodro says for existing students, blue bus cards are expected to be topped up automatically during Terms 2 and 3.

The Ministry says cards are topped up twice each term, covering Weeks 1 to 7 and Weeks 8 to 14.

The Minister says delays could result from incomplete applications or information not being submitted and verified within the required timeframe.

He asked Opposition MP Hem Chand to provide the Ministry with a list of affected students and their details so the cases could be investigated and processed.

The Minister also reminded students to keep their cards safe.

Students who lose or damage their cards must apply for a replacement through their school and have the replacement activated through the Ministry's FEMIS system.

Radrodro says the Government has allocated $54 million in the 2026–27 Budget for student transport assistance. The programme supports more than 70,000 students through blue bus cards and more than 44,000 st udents through Rural Service Licences.

With Term 3 approaching, the immediate concern remains whether students who have already applied but are still waiting for their cards will receive them in time to avoid fu rther transport costs for their families.
